tldr: No direct Canadian-bank moves today besides a minor RBC Insurance benefits launch. The news that matters comes from the edges: tokenized stocks, agentic checkout, longer trading hours and wallet expansion are all raising customer expectations, while Latin American players tinker with fees and card perks.
themes: AI agents in payments and analytics
Fee restructuring (flat annual fees, funding-method cuts)
Travel-points and Black Friday card offers

highlights.headline: OKX and NYSE parent ICE launch a tokenized stock venue with 113 assets lined up; Nasdaq is also publishing a 23/5 trading information hub
highlights.why: Tokenized equities and near-round-the-clock trading are becoming mainstream. This is a signal for Simplii's brokerage roadmap (Direct Investing hours, product scope) to consider.

highlights.headline: Klarna is now available when an AI agent checks out through Adyen Agentic, and Expensify launched AI-powered Insights
highlights.why: Agent-initiated payments and AI analytics are moving from concept to live product. Simplii should consider how its cards and accounts will work in agentic checkout, and whether to offer spend insights.

highlights.headline: Google Wallet launched on iOS across the US
highlights.why: Wallet competition on iPhone is widening. It is worth checking how Simplii's cards provision and perform across wallets, and whether wallet features could pull customers away from bank apps.

highlights.headline: Mercado Bitcoin is replacing its inactivity fee with a flat R$46.80 annual fee for all customers, and Mercado Pago is dropping debit cards as a way to add funds from December
highlights.why: Fee and funding-method changes at fintechs show how providers are cutting cost-to-serve. They also show the customer backlash risk Simplii should weigh before changing no-fee positioning or funding options.
